subject: Character sets
notes: kb/Work PB929 sweep (2026-10-25): re-verdicted PARTIAL -> CONFORMS because the reason the row carried no longer reproduces on this tree. Rule sentence: cite.py --check 8.1.2 "The number of bytes used to represent a character of the national coded character set shall be equal to or greater than the number of bytes used to represent a character of the alphanumeric coded character set" -> OK 8.1.2 3). National 2 >= alphanumeric 1 (a USAGE DISPLAY character is one byte, a USAGE NATIONAL character two), pinned by l1_usage_display_character_size (its LEQN line compares BYTE-LENGTH of X(1) and N(1)). The row text's trailing implementor obligations are each documented and pinned now: bits per byte, A.1 item 12 (DOC-A.1-12); the one alphanumeric coded character value of each COBOL element, item 32 (DOC-A.1-32, goldens l1c05_coded_character_values); the additional characters prohibited as a currency symbol, item 44 (DOC-A.1-44, golden l1c06_currency_non_cobol_symbols); hex literals and the repertoire, items 33/34/95 (DOC-A.1-33, DOC-A.1-34, DOC-A.1-95). The premise that the alphanumeric character is one byte, which the earlier PARTIAL called undermined by GR-8.1.2-1, is restored: GR-8.1.2-1 CONFORMS (kb/Work PB547 landed).
